A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Disentangling Representations through Multi-task Learning. The complete main texts, appendices, equations, figures and tables are readable and support matching retained, revised and added material.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments with RNNs, LSTMs and GPT-2, including generalization scores, representation geometry and robustness analyses in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds results on quadratic observation-map nonlinearities and quantitative sparsity in Appendices A.5 and A.12.

M1.justification: The multi-task classification procedure, trained architectures, objectives and linear probing method remain unchanged. The quadratic encoder experiment varies the fixed observation-generating map to test robustness; it does not introduce a new learning algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix A.5 adds an input scenario using quadratic observation-map nonlinearities, extending evaluation beyond the original ReLU mapping. The synthetic latent distributions and existing classification, interleaved-learning and reaction-time tasks are retained.

E2.justification: Matched comparisons retain RNNs, non-leaky RNNs, LSTMs, GPT-2 and the context-dependent computation comparison. No comparator is added to or removed from these experiments; the new sparsity analysis reuses existing recurrent architectures.

E3.justification: The new sparsity analysis samples 1,000 ground-truth vectors per network, computes a response-sparseness score for each neuron and averages across neurons. Existing decoder splits, training budgets, transformer configurations and Table S1 settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds a ReLU-versus-quadratic observation-map robustness test and a systematic sparsity analysis across task count, latent dimensionality and recurrent architecture. These refine existing robustness and sparsity claims; the earlier noise, correlation, interleaving and reaction-time analyses remain.

E5.justification: The new reproducibility statement explicitly says the experiments are seeded. Five networks per configuration, repeated decoder fits and percentile reporting were already documented in v2 Appendices A.2–A.3; there is no documented increase in repetitions.

E6.justification: New Figure S1 reports virtually identical OOD generalization for quadratic and ReLU observation maps. New Figure S6 reports approximately 90% sparsity for RNNs and non-leaky RNNs, lower sparsity for LSTMs, and decreasing RNN sparsity with increasing latent dimensionality. Existing main results, including median OOD/ID r-squared values of 0.96/0.97, are retained.

T1.justification: Theorems B.5–B.6 replace the earlier mutual-information/entropy argument with explicit reconstruction and sufficient-statistic reasoning, while B.4–B.5 explicitly require Ntask >= D. New Corollary B.7 specifies assumptions and an approximate O(1/sqrt(Ntask)) recovery-rate assertion for suboptimal classifiers. v3 also corrects the tanh approximation statement and the extra transpose factor in the sigmoid reconstruction formula. These substantively revise the theoretical support.

C1.justification: The abstract explicitly qualifies the guarantees as applying to affine boundaries in latent space and reframes the contribution as linking multi-task competence to world models. The introduction emphasizes independence from the training paradigm. The principal disentanglement, noise, continuous-attractor and transformer claims remain.

C2.justification: Appendix A.14 substantially expands the biological interpretation: competence need not require simultaneous behavioral actions or simultaneous external supervision, because previously learned tasks can continue constraining representations. Additional discussion connects this account to replay, interprets distillation as transferring world models, and explains sparsity through representational capacity. Existing factorization and benchmark limitations are retained in the expanded Appendix A.15.

D1.justification: v3 adds an explicit code-repository link and reproducibility statement, and clarifies that the fixation input is concatenated with encoded observations. Existing hyperparameters and GPT-2 implementation details are retained. The PDFs establish added access information, not independently verified repository availability.

R1.justification: v3 adds references concerning activation-dependent geometry, multi-task disentanglement, information theory, sparsity and biological memory/replay. These support targeted contextual expansions; the central positioning relative to Johnston and Fusi, Lachapelle and other prior disentanglement work remains.

P1.justification: v3 revises the abstract and theoretical exposition, adds a proof roadmap, reproducibility and author-contribution statements, and moves the limitations discussion into Appendix A.15. Terminology and citations are edited, but most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figures S1 and S6, annotates and relocates Figure 2, and redisplays the Gaussian-CDF approximation plot with a revised legend. It adopts conference headers and typography and adjusts captions and figure placement. The main empirical figures and hyperparameter table retain their displays.

improvement.justification: The revised reconstruction proofs remove v2's unsupported mutual-information/entropy equality and correct mathematical expressions. The targeted robustness and sparsity analyses strengthen existing claims, while code and seed disclosures improve auditability. These are useful but bounded gains: the main empirical findings remain unchanged, and the new recovery-rate assertion in Corollary B.7 lacks a detailed error-propagation derivation.
